# Assessment rules

<!-- Generated by `go run ./cmd/gendocs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Soliton Rudder's cluster assessment runs 36 built-in, read-only checks against a snapshot of your cluster.
This page lists every check, what it looks for, how severe a finding can be, and how to fix it.
See the [user guide](USER-GUIDE.md#assessments) for how scoring works.

System namespaces (`kube-*`) are excluded from workload hygiene and security checks. Workload checks run once per
Deployment / StatefulSet / DaemonSet / CronJob / Job template (and bare pods), not once per replica.
Checks that need metrics-server are skipped (and reported as skipped) when it is not installed.

## Resources

### Node resource requests near capacity

`node-request-saturation` · severity: medium (≥85%) · high (≥100%)

Pod CPU/memory requests are close to (or above) a node's allocatable resources, leaving no room to schedule or burst.

**How to fix:** Add nodes, move workloads, or right-size requests. Above 100% pods stay Pending.

### Capacity to survive losing a node

`cluster-headroom` · severity: high · medium (single-node cluster)

Checks whether the remaining nodes could host all requested resources if the largest node failed.

**How to fix:** Add capacity so requests fit without the largest node (N+1), or reduce requests.

### Containers without resource requests

`no-requests` · severity: medium

Containers with no CPU or memory request are scheduled blindly and are the first to be evicted.

**How to fix:** Set resources.requests for cpu and memory on every container.

### Containers without a memory limit

`no-memory-limit` · severity: low

A container without a memory limit can consume a whole node's memory and trigger evictions.

**How to fix:** Set resources.limits.memory (usually close to the request).

### Pods using most of their memory limit

`memory-near-limit` · severity: high

Pods running at 90%+ of their memory limit are at risk of being OOMKilled.

**How to fix:** Raise the memory limit or reduce memory use.

### Over-provisioned pods

`overprovisioned` · severity: low

Pods using under 10% of their CPU or memory requests waste schedulable capacity.

**How to fix:** Lower the requests to match real usage (leave headroom for peaks).

## Reliability

### Unhealthy or cordoned nodes

`node-health` · severity: critical (NotReady) · high (pressure) · low (cordoned)

Nodes that are NotReady, under pressure or cordoned reduce capacity and can evict pods.

**How to fix:** Investigate kubelet/network/disk on the node, or uncordon if the maintenance is finished.

### Single-replica workloads

`single-replica` · severity: medium · high (production namespace)

Deployments and StatefulSets with one replica have downtime during node drains, upgrades and failures.

**How to fix:** Run at least 2 replicas for anything that should stay available.

### Replicated workloads without a PodDisruptionBudget

`no-pdb` · severity: low · medium (production namespace)

Without a PDB, voluntary disruptions (drains, upgrades) may take down all replicas at once.

**How to fix:** Create a PodDisruptionBudget (e.g. minAvailable: 1) selecting the workload.

### Containers without readiness probes

`no-readiness-probe` · severity: medium

Without a readiness probe traffic is sent to pods before they can serve it, and rollouts cannot detect bad versions.

**How to fix:** Add a readinessProbe to long-running containers.

### Containers without liveness probes

`no-liveness-probe` · severity: low

Without a liveness probe a hung process (deadlock, stuck event loop) keeps running and serving errors until someone notices.

**How to fix:** Add a livenessProbe that detects a stuck process, with a generous timeout so it never restarts a merely slow one.

### Probes pointing at undeclared ports

`probe-misconfigured` · severity: medium

A probe that targets a port the container does not declare (or a port name that does not exist) usually fails or checks the wrong endpoint, causing restarts or traffic to unready pods.

**How to fix:** Point the probe at a port the container actually listens on and declare it under ports.

### Autoscalers at their maximum

`hpa-maxed` · severity: medium

HorizontalPodAutoscalers already running at maxReplicas cannot absorb more load.

**How to fix:** Raise maxReplicas (and check node capacity) or optimise the workload.

### Crashing or failing-to-start pods

`crashing-pods` · severity: high · medium (many restarts)

Pods in CrashLoopBackOff, image pull errors, config errors or with many restarts.

**How to fix:** Open the pod's Health and Logs (Previous) in Soliton Rudder to find the cause.

### Workloads with unavailable replicas

`unhealthy-workloads` · severity: high (none ready) · medium (some ready)

Deployments, StatefulSets or DaemonSets where fewer replicas are ready than desired.

**How to fix:** Check the workload's pods, events and rollout status.

### Pods stuck in Pending

`stuck-pending` · severity: medium

Pods Pending for over 10 minutes usually cannot be scheduled (resources, taints, affinity, volumes).

**How to fix:** Check the pod's Scheduling health check and the cluster's free capacity.

### Failed or evicted pods lingering

`failed-pods` · severity: low

Pods in Failed phase (often Evicted) that nobody cleaned up hide real problems and clutter the cluster.

**How to fix:** Delete the failed pods and fix the cause (usually node pressure).

### Unbound PersistentVolumeClaims

`pending-pvc` · severity: medium

PVCs stuck in Pending block the pods that use them.

**How to fix:** Check the StorageClass, provisioner and available volumes.

### Replicas concentrated on one node

`replicas-one-node` · severity: medium

All replicas of a workload run on the same node, so a single node failure takes the service down.

**How to fix:** Use topologySpreadConstraints or pod anti-affinity to spread replicas.

### TLS certificates expiring or expired

`certificate-expiry` · severity: high (expired or < 14 days) · medium (< 30 days)

kubernetes.io/tls Secrets whose certificate has expired or expires within 30 days cause outages when it lapses.

**How to fix:** Renew the certificate (check cert-manager's Certificate/Issuer status) or replace the Secret. See the Certificates view.

## Security

### Privileged containers

`privileged` · severity: critical

Privileged containers have nearly full access to the host.

**How to fix:** Remove privileged: true; grant only the specific capabilities needed.

### Host network / PID / IPC sharing

`host-namespaces` · severity: high

Sharing host namespaces lets a container observe or interfere with the node and other pods.

**How to fix:** Remove hostNetwork, hostPID and hostIPC unless strictly required.

### hostPath volumes

`host-path` · severity: medium · high (root or container-runtime socket)

hostPath mounts expose node files to the container; mounting the root or the container runtime socket is equivalent to node access.

**How to fix:** Use emptyDir, PersistentVolumes or CSI volumes instead.

### Containers explicitly running as root

`run-as-root` · severity: high

runAsUser: 0 means a compromised process is root inside the container.

**How to fix:** Run as a non-root user (runAsNonRoot: true and a numeric runAsUser).

### Containers that may run as root

`no-run-as-nonroot` · severity: low

Without runAsNonRoot (or a non-zero runAsUser) the container runs as whatever user the image defines, often root.

**How to fix:** Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true and a numeric runAsUser; make sure the image supports it.

### Writable root filesystems

`no-readonly-rootfs` · severity: low

A writable root filesystem lets an attacker who gets code execution drop tools and persist changes inside the container.

**How to fix:** Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount emptyDir volumes for paths the app must write (e.g. /tmp).

### No seccomp profile

`no-seccomp` · severity: low

Without a seccomp profile the container may call any syscall the kernel allows, widening the attack surface.

**How to fix:** Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault on the pod.

### Privilege escalation not disabled

`privilege-escalation` · severity: low

Containers that do not set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false can gain more privileges than their parent process.

**How to fix:** Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.

### Dangerous Linux capabilities

`dangerous-capabilities` · severity: high (ALL, SYS_ADMIN, …) · medium (NET_ADMIN, NET_RAW, …)

Capabilities such as SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN or ALL greatly widen the container's power.

**How to fix:** Drop ALL capabilities and add back only what is required.

### Images using :latest or no tag

`latest-tag` · severity: medium

Mutable tags make deployments non-reproducible and can silently pull unreviewed code.

**How to fix:** Pin images to a version tag or, better, a digest.

### Namespaces without NetworkPolicies

`no-network-policy` · severity: medium

Without any NetworkPolicy, every pod can talk to every other pod in the cluster.

**How to fix:** Add a default-deny policy and allow only the traffic you need.

### Ingress hosts without TLS

`ingress-no-tls` · severity: medium

Ingress hosts that are not covered by a TLS section serve traffic over plain HTTP.

**How to fix:** Add spec.tls with a certificate secret (e.g. via cert-manager).

## Maintenance

### Manifests using removed or deprecated APIs

`deprecated-apis` · severity: high (already removed) · medium (removal pending)

Objects last applied with API versions that were removed (or soon will be) fail when re-applied or after upgrades.

**How to fix:** Update the manifests to the supported apiVersion and re-apply.

### Node / control-plane version skew

`version-skew` · severity: high (>2 minors behind) · low

Kubelets older than the control plane by more than two minor versions are unsupported.

**How to fix:** Upgrade or replace the lagging nodes.

### Kubernetes version support

`k8s-support` · severity: high (unsupported) · low (oldest supported)

Upstream Kubernetes supports only the three most recent minor releases.

**How to fix:** Plan an upgrade to a supported minor version.

### Released or failed PersistentVolumes

`released-volumes` · severity: low

Volumes left in Released/Failed state keep costing money and hold stale data.

**How to fix:** Reclaim or delete the volumes once their data is no longer needed.

## Writing your own checks

Plugins can contribute additional rules; see the [plugin guide](PLUGINS.md).
